questions.question: The concept of five year plans of India was borrowed from _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Former Soviet Union**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The concept of **Five-Year Plans (FYPs)** in India was borrowed from the **Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR)**, commonly known as the **Former Soviet Union**.
 
• The **Soviet Union** was the first country in the world to implement a centralized economic plan, initiated by **Joseph Stalin** in **1928** to achieve rapid **industrialization**.
 
• Following India's independence, the first Prime Minister, **Jawaharlal Nehru**, who was deeply impressed by the **socialist economic model** and the success of **centralized planning** in the USSR, spearheaded the adoption of this system.
 
• To facilitate this, the **Planning Commission of India** was established on **March 15, 1950**, as a non-constitutional and advisory body to formulate the developmental strategies.
 
• The **First Five-Year Plan** was launched for the period **1951-1956**, focusing primarily on the **agricultural sector** to ensure food security and address the **refugee crisis** and **food shortages** after partition.
 
• This planning model aimed at the **balanced growth** of the economy through the **public sector**, regulating resources to meet national priorities over five-year cycles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Borrowings from other Nations:**

 
 
• **United Kingdom:** India adopted the **Parliamentary form of government**, the **Rule of Law**, **Single Citizenship**, and the **Bicameralism** system.
 
• **United States of America:** The Indian Constitution borrowed **Fundamental Rights**, **Judicial Review**, the **Preamble**, and the process of **Removal of Supreme Court and High Court judges**.
 
• **France:** The ideals of **Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity** inscribed in the **Preamble** and the **Republican structure** were taken from the **French Constitution**.
 
 
 
• **Transition to NITI Aayog:**
 
 
• The era of **Five-Year Plans** ended with the **Twelfth Five-Year Plan (2012-2017)**.
 
• On **January 1, 2015**, the **Planning Commission** was replaced by the **NITI Aayog** (National Institution for Transforming India) to promote **Cooperative Federalism** and a **Bottom-up approach**.

questions.question: Which type of cultivation did the Gonds practice primarily?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shifting cultivation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Gonds** are one of the largest tribal communities in **India**, traditionally inhabiting the vast forested region known as **Gondwana**, which covers parts of **Madhya Pradesh**, **Chhattisgarh**, **Maharashtra**, and **Odisha**.
 
• Historically, the **Gonds** primarily practiced **shifting cultivation**, a traditional agricultural method where patches of forest land are cleared by felling trees and burning them.
 
• This practice is locally known by various names such as **bewar**, **penda**, or **podu**; the resulting ash acts as a natural fertilizer, providing essential **nutrients** like **potash** to the soil.
 
• Seeds are scattered in the ashes after the first monsoon rains, and the land is cultivated for a few years until the **soil fertility** declines significantly.
 
• Once the yield decreases, the **Gond** farmers abandon the current plot and move to a new area of the forest, allowing the previous land to lie **fallow** and recover its natural vegetation over several years.
 
• This mobile system of agriculture was central to their **social structure** and **communal land ownership**, where the village community managed the forest resources collectively under a **Raja** or **Chieftain**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Terrace cultivation**:

 
 
• Commonly practiced in **mountainous regions** like the **Himalayas** or the **Western Ghats**.
 
• It involves carving **flat steps** or terraces into steep slopes to create arable land and prevent **soil erosion**.
 
 
 
• **Permanent farming**:
 
 
• Also known as **settled agriculture**, where farmers cultivate the same piece of land year after year.
 
• While the **Gonds** were traditionally shifting cultivators, many transitioned to **settled farming** during the **British colonial period** due to changes in **forest laws**.
 
 
 
• **Irrigation-based farming**:
 
 
• A system that relies on the artificial application of water through **canals**, **wells**, or **dams**.
 
• This intensive method is typical of **alluvial plains** and was not the primary mode of the forest-dwelling **Gond** economy.

questions.question: Article 53 of the Indian constitution is related with ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Executive power of the Union**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 53** of the **Constitution of India** establishes the framework for the **Union Executive**, declaring that the **executive power** shall be vested in the **President**.
 
• According to **Article 53(1)**, this power is exercised by the President either **directly** or through **officers subordinate** to him, adhering strictly to the provisions of the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• The **Supreme Command** of the **Defence Forces** (Army, Navy, and Air Force) is formally vested in the President under **Article 53(2)**, though its exercise is regulated by law passed by **Parliament**.
 
• While the **legal authority** is vested in the President, **Article 74** necessitates that the President acts on the **aid and advice** of the **Council of Ministers**, headed by the **Prime Minister**.
 
• This article effectively makes the President the **De jure** (titular) head of the state, while the actual **executive administration** is managed by the **Cabinet**.
 
• **Article 53(3)** clarifies that the vesting of power in the President does not prevent **Parliament** from conferring by law functions on authorities other than the President, nor does it transfer powers already held by **State Governments**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Term of office of President**:

 
 
• Under **Article 56**, the President holds office for a term of **five years** from the date of assumption of duties.
 
• The President can resign by writing to the **Vice-President** or be removed via **impeachment** for violating the Constitution under **Article 61**.
 
 
 
• **Qualifications for election as President**:
 
 
• **Article 58** prescribes that a person must be a **citizen of India**, have completed **35 years** of age, and be qualified for election as a member of the **Lok Sabha**.
 
• The individual must not hold any **office of profit** under the **Government of India**, State Governments, or any local authority.
 
 
 
• **Election of President**:
 
 
• **Article 54** mandates that the President is elected by an **electoral college** consisting of elected members of both Houses of **Parliament** and elected members of the **Legislative Assemblies** (MLAs) of the States and Union Territories (Delhi and Puducherry).
 
• The election follows the system of **proportional representation** by means of a **single transferable vote**.

questions.question:
In 2025 India marked 10 years of the AMRUT initiative.

Which is the nodal ministry for the AMRUT initiative?

options.text: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT)** was launched by the Government of India in **June 2015**, with the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)** serving as the nodal ministry.
 
• The mission aims to provide basic services like **water supply**, **sewerage**, and **urban transport** to households and build amenities in cities to improve the quality of life, focusing specifically on the poor and disadvantaged.
 
• The mission initially targeted **500 cities** across India, covering approximately **60 percent** of the urban population.
 
• The initiative emphasizes **Green Spaces** and parks, **Stormwater drainage** to reduce flooding, and **Non-motorized Urban Transport** such as cycling and pedestrian facilities.
 
• In **October 2021**, **AMRUT 2.0** was launched to make cities **water secure** and provide 100 percent coverage of water supply to all households in around **4,700 statutory towns**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)**:

 
 
• This ministry was formed by merging the **Ministry of Urban Development** and the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation** in **July 2017**.
 
• It administers other major schemes like the **Smart Cities Mission**, **Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban (SBM-U)**, and **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban (PMAY-U)**.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Jal Shakti**:
 
 
• Created in **May 2019** by merging the Ministry of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation, and the Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation.
 
• It manages the **Jal Jeevan Mission**, which primarily focuses on providing **Functional Household Tap Connections (FHTC)** in rural India.
 
 
 
• **Funding Mechanism**:
 
 
• AMRUT is a **Centrally Sponsored Scheme** where the **Central Government** provides a significant portion of the funds, while the rest is shared by **State Governments** and **Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)** based on city population.

questions.question: Which of the following is INCORRECT about peninsular plateau of India?

options.text: It lies in the south of northern plains.
Aravalli hills, one of the oldest ranges of the world, border it on the north-west side.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The relief is highly even.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Peninsular Plateau** is a tableland located to the south of the **Northern Plains**, extending up to the southern tip of the Indian mainland. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The plateau is broadly **triangular** in shape, with its base aligned with the southern edge of the **Indo-Gangetic plains** and its apex at **Kanniyakumari**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• The relief of the **Peninsular Plateau** is not even; it is highly **rugged** and **undulating**, characterized by numerous **plateaus**, **hill ranges**, and **deep river valleys**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Aravalli Hills**, which are among the **oldest fold mountains** in the world, form the north-western boundary of the plateau. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Peninsular Plateau**:

 
 
• **Geological Origin**: It was formed due to the breaking and drifting of the **Gondwana land**, making it one of the **oldest** and most stable landmasses of the **Earth crust**.
 
• **Major Divisions**: It is primarily divided into two parts: the **Central Highlands** (north of the Narmada river) and the **Deccan Plateau** (south of the Narmada river).
 
• **Rock Composition**: The region is composed of **crystalline**, **igneous**, and **metamorphic rocks**, featuring rounded hills and wide valleys.
 
• **Black Soil Area**: One of the distinct features of this plateau is the **Deccan Trap**, which is a region of **volcanic origin** characterized by **black soil** suitable for cotton cultivation.
 
• **Aravalli Range**: These hills are highly **eroded** and appear as **broken hills**, extending from **Gujarat** through **Rajasthan** to **Delhi**.

questions.question:
Which of the following is a social development scheme in India?

I. PM-AJAY

II. SMILE scheme
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY)** is a comprehensive scheme launched to uplift the socio-economic status of the **Scheduled Castes (SC)** population by merging three existing initiatives: **Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana (PMAGY)**, **Special Central Assistance to Scheduled Castes Sub Plan (SCA to SCSP)**, and **Babu Jagjivan Ram Chhatrawas Yojana (BJRCY)**. It focuses on reducing poverty through infrastructure development, skill training, and income-generating schemes. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• The **SMILE (Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise)** scheme is a central sector initiative formulated by the **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment**. It provides a legal and social framework for the **comprehensive rehabilitation** of two specific groups: **Transgender Persons** and individuals engaged in the act of **begging**. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment**: This is the nodal ministry for implementing both the **PM-AJAY** and **SMILE** schemes, ensuring inclusive growth for the most marginalized sections of Indian society.
 
• **PM-AJAY Components**:
 
 
• **Adarsh Gram**: Aims to provide essential infrastructure in villages having an **SC population** of 50% or more.
 
• **Grant-in-Aid**: Financial assistance for district-level projects that promote **livelihood** and **socio-economic** development.
 
 
 
• **SMILE Sub-schemes**:
 
 
• **Rehabilitation of Transgender Persons**: Includes provisions for **Scholarships**, **Skill Development**, and **Garima Greh** (shelter homes) to provide a safe space for the community.
 
• **Rehabilitation for Begging**: Focuses on **survey and identification**, **medical facilities**, and **re-integration** into mainstream society through vocational training.

questions.question: Article 256 of the Indian Constitution is related with which of the following?

options.text: Power of the Union to confer powers, etc., on States in certain cases
Obligation of States and the Union
Jurisdiction of the Union in relation to territories outside India
Power of the States to entrust functions to the Union

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Obligation of States and the Union**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 256** of the **Indian Constitution** stipulates that the **executive power** of every State shall be so exercised as to ensure compliance with the laws made by **Parliament** and any existing laws which apply in that State.
 
• It explicitly outlines the **Obligation of States and the Union**, where the **Union executive** is empowered to give such directions to a State as may appear to the **Government of India** to be necessary for the purpose of ensuring legal compliance.
 
• This provision serves as a fundamental pillar of **Administrative Relations** between the Centre and the States, ensuring that the **federal structure** functions harmoniously under the **supremacy of Central legislation**.
 
• The article is located within **Part XI** of the Constitution, which governs the **Relations between the Union and the States**, specifically under **Chapter II** regarding **Administrative Relations**.
 
• Non-compliance with the directions issued under **Article 256** can invoke **Article 365**, which empowers the **President** to conclude that the State government cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 258**:

 
 
• Relates to the **Power of the Union to confer powers**, etc., on States in certain cases.
 
• It allows the **President**, with the consent of the State government, to entrust either conditionally or unconditionally to that Government functions in relation to any matter to which the **executive power of the Union** extends.
 
 
 
• **Article 260**:
 
 
• Relates to the **Jurisdiction of the Union in relation to territories outside India**.
 
• It permits the **Government of India** to undertake any executive, legislative, or judicial functions of a territory not being part of India by agreement with the Government of that territory.
 
 
 
• **Article 258A**:
 
 
• Relates to the **Power of the States to entrust functions to the Union**.
 
• This was inserted by the **7th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956**, allowing the **Governor** of a State, with the consent of the **Government of India**, to entrust functions to the Union.
 
 
 
• **Article 257**:
 
 
• Deals with the **Control of the Union over States** in certain cases, particularly regarding the maintenance of **means of communication** of national or military importance.

questions.question: Which of the following Indian state/Union Territory practices the folk dance form 'Ranmale'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ranmale** is a traditional ritualistic **folk theater** and dance form predominantly practiced in the **Sattari** and **Sanguem** talukas of **Goa**, as well as parts of neighboring **Sindhudurg** in **Maharashtra**.
 
• It is traditionally performed by the **agricultural** and **forest-dwelling communities**, primarily the **Zorman** community, during the **Shigmo** festival, which marks the arrival of spring.
 
• The performance is a fusion of dance, drama, and music, where participants enact stories from the **Indian epics**, specifically the **Ramayana** and the **Mahabharata**.
 
• Historically, **Ranmale** served as a medium of entertainment and socio-religious expression for the rural population residing in the **Western Ghats** region.
 
• The musical elements are vital to the performance, featuring traditional instruments like the **Ghumat** (a terracotta pot drum), **Shamel**, and **Cymbals** to provide a rhythmic base for the dancers.
 
• The dance takes place in a sacred community space known as the **Mand**, often performed under the illumination of traditional oil torches or lamps.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Telangana**:

 
 
• Home to the **Perini Shivatandavam**, an ancient dance form known as the **Dance of Warriors**, which flourished during the **Kakatiya dynasty**.
 
• **Lambadi** is another prominent folk dance performed by the nomadic **Banjara** tribes of the state.
 
 
 
• **Manipur**:
 
 
• Famous for **Manipuri**, one of the eight **classical dances** of India, which often focuses on the **Raas Leela** (the divine love of Radha and Krishna).
 
• The state also features **Pung Cholom**, a unique dance involving acrobatic movements and the use of the **Pung** drum.
 
 
 
• **Jammu and Kashmir**:
 
 
• Known for the **Rouf** dance, a popular folk dance performed by women during festive occasions like **Eid** and the harvesting season.
 
• **Bacha Nagma** and **Dumhal** are other traditional performances deeply rooted in the cultural fabric of the **Kashmir Valley**.

questions.question: In 2025, ____ species, Zographetus mathewi, has been discovered in Western ghats.
questions.solution:
__Concept:__

The **Western Ghats** is a globally recognized **biodiversity hotspot** where new species are frequently discovered. Taxonomic classification helps identify these species based on their **morphological** and **genetic** characteristics, which is essential for **wildlife conservation**.

Given

Discovery Year: **2025**

Species Name: **Zographetus mathewi**

Region: **Western Ghats**

Information

In early **2025**, researchers identified a new species named **Zographetus mathewi**. This species belongs to the **Hesperiidae** family, which comprises **skippers**, a group of **butterflies**. The discovery was made in the **Aralam Wildlife Sanctuary**, located in the **Kannur** district of **Kerala**. Commonly referred to as the **Aralam Forest Hopper**, the species is named in honor of **Mathew P. John** for his significant contributions to the field of **lepidopterology** (the study of butterflies and moths). Given its biological classification within the genus **Zographetus**, it is categorized as a **butterfly**.

Final Answer: ✅ butterfly

questions.question: The Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station is in ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS)** is a premier spaceport operated by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**.
 
• It is located in **Thumba**, a suburb of **Thiruvananthapuram**, which is the capital city of **Kerala**.
 
• The facility was established on **November 21, 1963**, marking the birth of the **Indian Space Programme**.
 
• **Thumba** was chosen for its strategic geographical location, as it lies very close to the **Earth magnetic equator** (dip equator), making it ideal for **ionospheric** and **electrojet** research.
 
• The first rocket launched from this station was a **Nike-Apache** sounding rocket, which was provided by **NASA** in the **United States**.
 
• In **1968**, the station was formally dedicated to the **United Nations** to facilitate international scientific cooperation in **aeronomy** and **upper atmospheric physics**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC)**:

 
 
• **TERLS** eventually evolved into the **Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre**, the lead **ISRO** center for the development of **satellite launch vehicles** like **PSLV**, **GSLV**, and **LVM3**.
 
• It was renamed in honor of **Dr. Vikram Sarabhai**, who is widely regarded as the **Father of the Indian Space Programme**.
 
 
 
• **Karnataka**:
 
 
• This state hosts the **ISRO Headquarters** and the **U R Rao Satellite Centre (URSC)** in **Bengaluru**, where major **satellite technology** developments occur.
 
 
 
• **Gujarat**:
 
 
• Home to the **Space Applications Centre (SAC)** in **Ahmedabad**, focusing on **remote sensing**, **communications**, and **satellite navigation** payloads.
 
 
 
• **Maharashtra**:
 
 
• Includes significant scientific institutions like the **Indian Institute of Geomagnetism (IIG)** in **Mumbai**, which researches **geomagnetic fields** relevant to space science.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is NOT correct?

options.text: Sliding friction is smaller than static friction.
Friction depends on how hard the two surfaces press together.
Friction is important for many of our activities.
Friction can be decreased by making the surface rough.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Friction can be decreased by making the surface rough.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Static Friction** occurs when surfaces are at rest relative to each other, allowing microscopic **irregularities** to interlock deeply. Once movement begins, the surfaces slide over each other without sufficient time for deep interlocking, making **Sliding Friction** generally lower than the maximum static friction. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• Frictional force is directly proportional to the **Normal Force**. If the force pressing the two surfaces together increases, the interlocking between the irregularities becomes more intense, thereby increasing the resistance to motion. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• Friction is vital for fundamental daily tasks such as **walking** (providing grip on the ground), **writing** (allowing the lead or ink to stick to paper), and **braking** (enabling vehicles to stop safely). ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• Friction arises from the **interlocking** of surface imperfections. Increasing the roughness of a surface adds more hills and valleys, which heightens the degree of interlocking and subsequently **increases friction** rather than decreasing it. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Friction:**

 
 
• **Static Friction:** The opposing force that prevents the initiation of motion between two surfaces.
 
• **Sliding Friction:** Also known as kinetic friction, it acts when one surface is actually sliding over another.
 
• **Rolling Friction:** Occurs when an object rolls over a surface; it is significantly weaker than sliding friction, which is why **Wheels** and **Ball Bearings** are used in machinery.
 
• **Fluid Friction:** Often called **Drag**, it is the resistance offered by liquids and gases to objects moving through them.
 
 
 
• **Methods to Modify Friction:**
 
 
• **Lubrication:** Applying substances like **Oil**, **Grease**, or **Graphite** fills the surface irregularities, creating a thin layer that reduces direct contact.
 
• **Polishing:** Making surfaces smoother to minimize the height of microscopic bumps.
 
• **Treading:** Tires and shoes are designed with **Treads** and **Spikes** specifically to increase friction for better grip.

questions.question: The verses of Saint Kabir are mainly found in which famous collection?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bijak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Saint Kabir** was a legendary 15th-century mystic poet and saint of the **Bhakti movement** whose teachings fundamentally influenced the religious landscape of Northern India and the foundation of **Sikhism**.
 
• The **Bijak** is considered the most authentic and authoritative compilation of Kabir’s verses, serving as the primary holy scripture for the **Kabir Panth** sect.
 
• It is traditionally divided into three distinct sections: **Sakhi** (witnessing couplets teaching moral truths), **Shabda** (hymns meant for singing), and **Ramaini** (longer poems dealing with metaphysical and spiritual doctrines).
 
• Kabir utilized a unique linguistic style known as **Sadhukkari Bhasha**, which integrated elements of **Awadhi**, **Braj**, **Bhojpuri**, and **Punjabi** to communicate with the common masses.
 
• His poetry strongly advocated for **Nirguna Bhakti** (devotion to a formless God) and criticized organized religious rituals, the **caste system**, and the hypocrisy of the clergy in both Hinduism and Islam.
 
• Beyond the Bijak, a significant number of his verses are preserved in the **Kabir Granthavali** (Rajasthan tradition) and the **Guru Granth Sahib**, which contains over **500 verses** attributed to him.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Padavali**

 
 
• This refers to a genre of devotional songs, most famously the **Vidyapati Padavali** composed by the 14th-century poet **Vidyapati** in the **Maithili** language.
 
• The verses primarily revolve around the divine and romantic love between **Radha** and **Lord Krishna**.
 
 
 
• **Gitagovinda**
 
 
• A renowned 12th-century Sanskrit work composed by the poet **Jayadeva**, who served in the court of the **Sena dynasty** in Bengal.
 
• It describes the intricate relationship and the emotional pangs of separation between **Krishna** and the **Gopis**, particularly **Radha**.
 
 
 
• **Prabandha Chintamani**
 
 
• A semi-historical Sanskrit text authored by the Jain scholar **Merutunga** in **1304 CE**.
 
• It provides valuable historical anecdotes and biographical accounts of medieval Indian kings, including **Bhoja** of the Paramara dynasty and **Siddharaja Jaisimha** of Gujarat.

questions.question: In a candle middle zone of partial combustion is of which colour?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Yellow**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A candle flame is divided into three distinct regions based on the availability of **oxygen** and the extent of **combustion**: the innermost, middle, and outer zones.
 
• The **middle zone** is the region where **partial combustion** (or incomplete combustion) occurs because the supply of air is limited in this central area.
 
• In this zone, the **wax vapors** do not burn completely, leading to the formation of **unburnt carbon particles**.
 
• These tiny **carbon particles** get heated to a high temperature and begin to glow, a process known as **incandescence**, which gives the flame its characteristic **yellow color**.
 
• Due to the emission of light from these glowing particles, the middle zone is also referred to as the **luminous zone** of the flame.
 
• Temperature-wise, the middle zone is considered **moderately hot**, sitting between the temperature extremes of the innermost and outermost layers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Outer Zone of Complete Combustion:**

 
 
• This is the **hottest part** of the candle flame where there is an abundant supply of **oxygen**.
 
• It undergoes **complete combustion**, resulting in a **blue color** flame that is **non-luminous**.
 
• Goldsmiths often use this part of the flame with a **metallic blowpipe** to melt gold and silver.
 
 
 
• **Innermost Zone of Unburnt Vapors:**
 
 
• This area immediately surrounds the **wick** and contains **unburnt wax vapors**.
 
• It appears **black** in color and is the **coolest part** (least hot) of the entire flame.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Composition:**
 
 
• Candle wax is primarily composed of **hydrocarbons** like **paraffin wax**.
 
• The process of burning involves the **vaporization** of liquid wax through **capillary action** up the wick.

questions.question: Which BARC developed reactor achieved first criticality with LEU fuel?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**APSARA-U**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **APSARA-U** (Apsara-Upgraded) is a high-performance **swimming pool-type** research reactor designed and built indigenously at the **Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC)**, Trombay.
 
• The reactor achieved its **first criticality** on **September 10, 2018**, making it the first research reactor in India to operate successfully using **Low Enriched Uranium (LEU)** fuel.
 
• The core of **APSARA-U** utilizes **indigenously developed** **Uranium silicide (U₃Si₂)** fuel dispersed in an **Aluminum matrix**, with **U-235** enrichment kept below 20 percent to meet international non-proliferation standards.
 
• It replaces the original **Apsara** reactor, which was **Asia’s first** research reactor (commissioned in **1956**) and previously functioned using **Highly Enriched Uranium (HEU)** fuel supplied by the **United Kingdom**.
 
• This upgraded facility provides a significantly higher **thermal neutron flux**, which is critical for the production of **medical radioisotopes** (such as **Iodine-131**), advanced **neutron activation analysis**, and **material science** research.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **DHRUVA**:

 
 
• Commissioned at **Trombay** in **1985**, it is India’s largest research reactor and uses **Natural Uranium** as fuel with **Heavy Water (D₂O)** as the moderator and coolant.
 
 
 
• **KAMINI**:
 
 
• Located at the **Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR)**, it is the only reactor in the world currently using **Uranium-233** fuel derived from **Thorium**.
 
 
 
• **PURNE (PURNIMA Series)**:
 
 
• The **PURNIMA** (Plutonium Reactor for Neutron Investigations in Multiplying Assemblies) reactors were experimental fast reactors at **BARC**; **PURNIMA-I** achieved criticality in **1972** using **Plutonium oxide** fuel.

questions.question: At the Olympic Games, the matches in a team event in table tennis is a best of ____ affair.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• At the **Olympic Games**, the team event in table tennis is conducted as a **best-of-five** matches competition, where the first team to win **three individual matches** wins the overall tie.
 
• The team event format was officially introduced at the **2008 Beijing Olympics**, replacing the separate doubles competition that had been a part of the program since 1988.
 
• Each team consists of **three athletes**. A match tie begins with a **doubles match**, which is immediately followed by a series of **singles matches** until a winner is decided.
 
• The standard order of play in the Olympic format is: Match 1 (**Doubles**), Match 2 (**Singles**), Match 3 (**Singles**), and if no team has won three matches yet, Match 4 (**Singles**) and Match 5 (**Singles**) are played.
 
• This **best-of-five** system ensures a balance between individual skill and team strategy, requiring players to be versatile in both singles and doubles formats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Match and Game Structure**:

 
 
• In the team event, each individual match (both singles and doubles) is typically played as a **best-of-five games**, whereas individual singles events at the Olympics are often **best-of-seven games**.
 
• A game is won by the first player or pair to reach **11 points**, provided there is at least a two-point margin of lead.
 
 
 
• **ITTF Regulations**:
 
 
• The **International Table Tennis Federation (ITTF)** is the world governing body that regulates the rules and equipment standards, including the **40mm diameter ball** and the **polymer (plastic) material** used in modern competition.
 
• Table tennis was first included in the **Olympic program** at the **1988 Seoul Games**.

questions.question: In hockey, the distance between the inner edges of the goalposts is ______ metres.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3.66**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **Field Hockey**, the dimensions of the goal are strictly regulated by the **International Hockey Federation (FIH)** to ensure global standardization of the sport.
 
• The distance between the **inner edges** of the vertical goalposts is precisely **3.66 metres**, which is equivalent to **4 yards** in the imperial system.
 
• The **goalposts** and the **crossbar** must have a rectangular cross-section with a width or thickness of **50 mm** (5 cm).
 
• The goalposts are positioned **centrally** on the **backlines**, and they must be **white** in color to provide maximum visibility against the playing surface.
 
• The measurement is taken between the **inner faces** of the posts, meaning the actual gap the ball must pass through is **3.66 metres** wide.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Goal Dimensions:**

 
 
• The height of the **crossbar** from the ground (lower edge) is **2.14 metres** (7 feet).
 
• The **goal nets** are attached to the posts and crossbar at intervals not exceeding **150 mm** to prevent the ball from passing through.
 
• **Sideboards** and **backboards** within the goal are **460 mm** high and are typically painted a dark color.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Football (Soccer):**
 
 
• The value **2.44** (metres) mentioned in the options is the standard **height** of an **Association Football** goal (8 feet).
 
• A standard **Football goal** is much wider than a hockey goal, measuring **7.32 metres** (8 yards) between the posts.
 
 
 
• **Field Dimensions:**
 
 
• A standard hockey pitch is **91.40 metres** long and **55.00 metres** wide.
 
• The **striking circle** (D-area) is a semi-circle with a radius of **14.63 metres** measured from the inner front corner of the goalposts.

questions.question: What was India's overall rank by total medal count at the 2018 Commonwealth Games?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3rd**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India secured the **3rd position** in the final medal standings at the **2018 Commonwealth Games**, which took place in **Gold Coast, Queensland, Australia**.
 
• Indian athletes delivered a stellar performance, clinching a total of **66 medals**, comprising **26 Gold**, **20 Silver**, and **20 Bronze** medals.
 
• This achievement stood as India's third-best demonstration in Commonwealth Games history, trailing behind the performances of the 2010 Delhi Games and the 2002 Manchester Games.
 
• **Shooting** emerged as the most successful sport for India, yielding **16 medals** (including 7 Gold), followed closely by **Wrestling** with 12 medals and **Weightlifting** with 9 medals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Overview of other top-performing countries at the 2018 Games:
 
 
• **Australia** dominated the tournament and finished in the **1st position** with a massive collection of **198 medals** (80 Gold, 59 Silver, and 59 Bronze).
 
• **England** took the **2nd position** on the leaderboard, accumulating **136 medals** (45 Gold, 45 Silver, and 46 Bronze).
 
• **Canada** finished in the **4th position**; despite winning 82 total medals, they stood behind India due to a lower gold medal count of 15 Gold.
